notes:
Inbound SMB: self-serve trial converted to discovery. Primary contact = Alex Kim (CTO). Main complaint: perceived slowness for chat responses in support UI. Key fragments from call:
- "Users feel the bot is slow after long conversations; sometimes session times out."
- Wants ~sub-300ms p50 for short replies (40-60 tokens) and p95 < 800ms if possible for majority of flows.
Observed from logs: median ~380ms for 120-token prompts, p95 ~1.2s when routed to eu-central. They defaulted to EU region via browser geolocation.
Customer constraints: wants public cloud hosted API, cost-sensitive (small SaaS budget), needs SSO and audit logs (SOC2 expected). No VPC/on-prem right now.
SE notes and quick recommendations passed to customer (Ravi):
- Try us-west region (us-west-2) for majority of NA users; observed 20-30% lower network RTT for their user base.
- Enable streaming responses to improve perceived latency (first-chunk TTFB often 2-3x faster than full-gen).
- Reduce prompt context: trim long system messages, paginate docs for doc-search instead of sending full doc. Aim for <150 tokens input when possible.
- Set client timeout to 30s (defaults were low in their SDK => led to dropped sessions); increase connection keepalive and use HTTP/2 multiplexing.
- Use smaller max_tokens for assistant replies where appropriate; move long-form generation to async background jobs.
- If cost vs perf tradeoff needed: try dev-mode with lower-cost model variants + routing fallback for non-critical queries.
Open items / followups:
- Customer to run a 48h trial in us-west with streaming on and share perf logs (Alex).
- Redwood to provide sample trimmed prompts and a short checklist for prompt-length vs latency tradeoffs.
- Confirm SOC2 audit scope and whether retention controls are required beyond default.
Notes are shorthand — expect more logs in INF-2337 ticket and security FAQ link on Drive.
use_case_summary: Support-chat + doc search. Primary UX constraint is perceived latency (fast single-turn replies). Throughput low (10-20 qps peak), but concurrency important during morning peaks. Model preference: smaller/fast variants for most queries, occasional larger model for complex summarization. Routing: prefer NA region, fallback to eu if capacity. Require audit logs + SSO.
